# Thesis memo

## Central thesis

A physical property is established across a family of descriptions only when
the transformations connecting them carry a proof object that identifies the
property's bearer, the class of probes on which it is tested, the structures
used by the inference, the approximation modulus, and the uniformity domain.
Manifest appearance in one representation is evidence about that
representation.  Transport to the physical theory additionally requires a
recovery theorem across every interface at which the property or one of its
logical prerequisites ceases to be explicit.

This is not generic model pluralism: the framework supplies a typed criterion
for when plural descriptions jointly establish one claim.  It is not the
slogan that physics is information: the framework can be stated without the
word *information*, using observables, states, maps, limits, and certificates.

## Formal anchor

The uniform recovery-to-spectrum theorem shows that a common Euclidean decay
rate does transport to a Hamiltonian spectral exclusion when positivity,
correlation recovery on a dense centered core, and index-uniform constants
are certified.  Three countermodels show that finite positivity, pointwise
recovery, or a nonseparating observable class does not suffice.

## Yang--Mills consequence

The framework changes the proof question from “where can a gap be seen?” to
“which representation generates a useful rigidity estimate, and which
certificates transport it through the continuum and reconstruction chain?”
It does not establish the open uniform bounds or the continuum construction.
